title: Extension popup UI
when: A browser extension needs a small window that opens from its toolbar button to show status or quick actions.
prompt:
Goal: A fast, accessible popup whose script lives in a file, loads state from storage on open and saves on every change, because the popup dies when it closes.
Steps:
1. manifest.json: "action": { "default_popup": "popup.html", "default_icon": { "16": "icons/16.png", "32": "icons/32.png" } }.
2. popup.html: <!doctype html>, <html lang="en">, <meta charset="utf-8">, a <main> with a heading, labeled controls, <button type="button">, and <script type="module" src="popup.js"></script>.
3. CSS: body width 320px to 380px, no fixed height; browsers cap popups near 800 by 600 pixels.
4. popup.js: const s = await chrome.storage.local.get({ enabled: true }); render, then attach listeners with addEventListener.
5. Save every change at once; blur closes the popup and its variables vanish.
6. Current page: const [tab] = await chrome.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true }); opening the popup grants activeTab.
7. Status text in an element with aria-live="polite"; prefers-color-scheme dark styles; visible :focus-visible outlines.
Quality bar:
- Opens instantly: no network on open, small script.
- Fully usable by keyboard.
Pitfalls:
- Inline <script> or onclick, both blocked by the extension CSP.
- State kept in popup variables and lost on blur.
- Long work started in the popup; hand it to the service worker.
Verify:
- [ ] Doctype, charset and lang.
- [ ] No inline handlers or scripts.
- [ ] Buttons have type="button".
- [ ] State saved on change.
Output: popup.html, popup.css, popup.js and the action entry in manifest.json.

examples.input: a popup with an on and off switch for my extension
examples.output: popup.html with labeled toggle and status, popup.js module reading and saving storage on change, 340px wide, dark mode
